text:
Mina: Noticing recurring tenant-level alerts: high split_rate and unexpected billing deltas for mixed-dim embedding batches. We should pick defaults for routing and preflight behavior.
Ravi: Yep. Is this mostly clients packing different dims in one request (e.g., 512 + 768 + 1536) or a lot of variable-length single vectors?
Mina: Mixed dims in a single vectors array. Example payload shape I pulled from logs: 
```
{"vectors":[{"id":"a","dim":768,...},{"id":"b","dim":1536,...},{"id":"c","dim":1024,...}]}
```
Splitter yields multiple chunks, sometimes reordering, sometimes 413. infra-bot flagged tenant T-77.
Oliver: Our splitter algorithm today is bytes-first to reduce chunk count; side-effect is large vectors go to front of routes and small ones wait -> tail latency for small dims.
Selena: From a console/UX POV, if we switch to a small-first fastpath, product needs a per-tenant metric: small_fastpath_util and estimated_units_delta so billing and SRE can correlate.
Jamie: Telemetry list suggestion: emit embed_split_count, embed_split_reason (enum bytes/dims/overflow), embed_units_estimate, embed_preflight_ms. Also tag each request with routing_policy={bytes-first,small-first,client-prechunk}.
Casey: API/runtime behavior proposal:
1) If ?preflight=true request -> respond with {units, split_plan} and HTTP 200; do not perform server-side splitting.
2) Default server-side behavior: try small-first contiguous selection that fits route_budget; else do best-effort split and attribute units per-chunk.
3) Hard limit: if anticipated split_count > 3 -> return 413 with guidance link.
Ravi: Example preflight API sketch:
POST /v1/embeddings?preflight=true
Body: {"vectors":[{"dim":768},{"dim":1536}], "prefer":"latency"}
Response: {"units":18, "split_plan":[{"start":0,"end":0,"route":"fast-768"},{"start":1,"end":1,"route":"batch-1536"}], "notes":"server-splitting-disabled"}
Mina: This helps customers that can re-chunk. But many expect server-side auto-split; we need conservative safe defaults to avoid surprise billing.
Selena: Console mock: route preview should show preflight units, toggle "auto-split server-side" with an info tooltip: "Server-side splitting may increase billed units. Use preflight to estimate and re-chunk client-side for best latency." Add a toast in Quota UI when a server-side split increases a request's estimated units by >20%.
Jamie: Rollout plan: behind feature flag `embed-adaptive-routing`. Phase 1: enable preflight and telemetry for 5% of tenants. Phase 2: enable small-first default for new tenants only. Phase 3: after 2 weeks of metrics bake, flip for all new tenants and make opt-in for legacy tenants.
Oliver: Runtime caveat: small-first affects queue coalescing and batching behavior; may increase CPU/kernel switches for large-homogenous workloads. We should fingerprint tenant workload and only apply small-first when mixed-dim score>threshold.
Casey: Safety fallback: if split_count > 3 OR cumulative_estimated_units > threshold -> refuse and return 413 with `Link` to admin preflight page. Also increment metric split_count_exceeded.{tenant}.
infra-bot: ALERT T-77: 30m window embed_split_rate=19%, avg_split_count=2.4, 413_count=10. See /alerts/1754339999/details
Ravi: Action items (owners): Runtime: add routing_policy toggle + emit policy tag (Oliver). API: spec preflight param and response (Ravi). Console: route preview, toggle, quota toast (Selena). Observability: new metrics + dashboard + paging alert rule (Jamie).
Selena: I'll produce three mock variants for the toggle & toast copy. Suggested concise tooltip copy: "Server-side splitting can increase billed units. Use preflight to preview cost and consider client-side re-chunking for lower latency."
Jamie: I'll create the dashboard card templates and an alert: tenant embed_split_rate>10% sustained 30m -> page on-call. Also chart preflight_usage vs split_rate.
Mina: Quick poll — objection to shipping preflight + small-first as default for new tenants (canary first)?
Oliver: No objection; prefer canary gating.
Casey: No objection.
Ravi: No objection.
Selena: No objection.
Jamie: No objection.
Mina: OK I'll file RFC + GH issues for runtime, api, console, telemetry and tag folks. We'll coordinate canary rollout schedule in next week's release planning. :thumbsup:
